title: Cross-Cloud Root or Global Admin Sign-In

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay or inject sample `aws:cloudtrail` events matching `*` into `index=cloud_multi`. Confirm UC-4.4.34 search returns >=1 row and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `*` markers. Confirm the search returns zero rows and alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=cloud_multi` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS + Microsoft Cloud Services + GCP (multi-index correlation); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Splunk Add-on for AWS + Microsoft Cloud Services + GCP (multi-index correlation)
spl:
index=cloud_multi sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.34_cross_cloud_root_or_glob_34"
| sort -_time
description: Correlates AWS root, Azure Global Admin, and GCP org admin logins within one hour.
value: Simultaneous super-admin use across clouds may indicate coordinated takeover. Detecting cross-cloud root or global admin sign-in early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=cloud_multi sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail.
visualization: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud_multi`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS + Microsoft Cloud Services + GCP (multi-index correlation) with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=cloud_multi sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud_multi sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud_multi sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.34_cross_cloud_root_or_glob_34"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=cloud_multi` to detect cross-cloud root or global admin sign-in. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_34_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS + Microsoft Cloud Services + GCP (multi-index correlation) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cross-cloud root or global admin sign-in so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
